chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Jew, the Christian, and the Magian should not swear by other than Allah, for indeed Allah says, 'And judge between them by what Allah has revealed.'

key_terms.وَ أَنِ اُحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَل: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Jews, Christians, and Magians swearing oaths by other than Allah?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians must not swear by entities other than Allah, grounding this in the Quranic command to judge them by what Allah revealed. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that while these communities have their own scriptures, their oaths derive authority from the Divine, and they are subject to the ultimate judgment of Allah's revelation. The reference to Surah Al-Ma'idah underscores the principle of *Hukm* (judgment) based on divine text, even for non-Muslims in their specific contexts.
